title: Expanding disease definitions in guidelines and expert panel ties to industry: a cross-sectional study of common conditions in the United States
authors: Moynihan RN, Cooke GP, Doust JA, Bero L, Hill S, Glasziou PP
population: The most recent publication, 2000 to 2013, from national and international panels setting definitions or diagnostic criteria for 14 common conditions in the United States (16 publications), including the JNC 7 hypertension report of 2003
funder: NHMRC Screening and Test Evaluation Program Grant. The funders had no role in study design, data collection and analysis, decision to publish, or preparation of the manuscript.
authorConflicts: Moynihan, Doust and Glasziou are involved in planning the Preventing Overdiagnosis conference; Hill chairs the Australian Pharmaceutical Benefits Advisory Committee and is on the PLOS Medicine editorial board; Bero declares none.
result: Ten of 16 publications widened disease definitions, one narrowed them and five had unclear impact; none rigorously assessed the potential harms of widening. Among 14 panels with disclosures, on average 75% of members had industry ties, 12 were chaired or led by people with ties, and members with ties had a median of seven companies. The JNC 7 hypertension panel created the category of pre-hypertension; 9 of its 11 members (82%) disclosed industry ties, to a median of 12 companies (IQR 11 to 13), its chair had ties, and 8 of 11 (73%) each had ties to Bristol-Myers Squibb, Merck and Novartis, whose products include irbesartan, losartan and amlodipine besylate/benazepril.
